mission_03: Neural Theorem Provers combine neural networks with symbolic theorem proving by learning inference rules in a differentiable manner. Instead of discrete symbolic manipulation, the prover operates on continuous truth values and learns rule parameters through gradient descent. Forward chaining propagates truth values through learned rules: each rule is parameterized as a weight matrix that transforms premise truth values into conclusion truth values via sigmoid activation. An inference network provides additional learned reasoning capacity. In this mission, you implement a neural theorem prover with rule embeddings, differentiable forward chaining that iteratively derives new facts, a prove function that checks if conclusions follow from premises, and a training loop that strengthens rules leading to correct conclusions using gradient-based updates.
